scope: Correct the epistemic status of the Tier-2 Vercel manual-snapshot carrier without modifying the actively changing retained PR810 controller lane.

source_a.surface: current Sandbox persistent-sandboxes documentation and Sandbox API/CLI documentation
source_a.observation: The current documentation surfaced by the connected Vercel documentation index says sandbox.delete permanently removes the named sandbox and sessions while snapshots remain until expiration or explicit snapshot deletion; snapshot deletion is separately addressable and Sandbox.create from an explicit snapshotId is documented.

source_b.surface: Knowledge Base guides updated 2026-06-29: How Vercel Sandbox duration and persistence work; The Complete Guide to Vercel Drives
source_b.observation: The duration/persistence guide says snapshots are tied to the sandbox lifecycle, and the Drives guide explicitly says deleting the producing sandbox also deletes its snapshots; it recommends a Drive when data must outlive the sandbox entirely.

official_documentation_conflict.possible_reconciliation_not_promoted: The conflict may reflect a distinction between manual snapshots and automatic persistent-sandbox snapshots or documentation drift, but this is only a hypothesis and is not treated as product truth.
official_documentation_conflict.promotion_rule: Neither categorical snapshot-survives-delete nor categorical snapshot-dies-with-delete receives canonical Tier-2 carrier truth from documentation alone. Exact authorized isolated runtime evidence decides the current SDK/API behavior.

cheapest_exact_runtime_discriminator.precondition: Use an authorized disposable Vercel Sandbox path bound to the exact controller/provider version; do not use VPS/self-hosted/production-host substitutes.
sequence: create a disposable source sandbox and record sandbox/session identity
write a non-secret random sentinel plus SHA-256 receipt in the declared transfer surface
create an explicit manual snapshot and record snapshot identity/status
delete the named source sandbox and confirm source identity is no longer retrievable/rejoinable
retrieve the exact snapshotId after source deletion and record its status
attempt Sandbox.create with source type snapshot, exact snapshotId, a distinct name/session and persistent:false
if creation succeeds, verify sentinel bytes/hash and prove replacement identity differs from source
delete the disposable replacement and explicitly delete the snapshot if it still exists
cheapest_exact_runtime_discriminator.pass_for_lifecycle_only: The exact post-delete snapshot remains retrievable and creates a distinct replacement containing the exact sentinel bytes/hash.
cheapest_exact_runtime_discriminator.fail_for_lifecycle_only: The snapshot is deleted/unavailable after source deletion or cannot instantiate the distinct replacement.
cheapest_exact_runtime_discriminator.tier2_credit: ZERO unless the later full declared-transfer, exact OCI identity, generation fencing, stale-writer rejection, effect no-replay, fresh secret reacquisition and second cognition gates also pass.

alternatives_if_snapshot_fails.vercel_drive: Architecturally provides an independent lifecycle according to current Vercel guidance, but is Private Beta and Vercel advises against production data use during beta; therefore it is not silently promoted as the canonical ClayVerse state carrier.
alternatives_if_snapshot_fails.external_durable_store: Requires separate explicit security, provenance, lifecycle, cost and owner-policy admission; it must remain a data carrier rather than a second ClayVerse state authority.

unusual_experiment.reason: The shared go macro-cycle already has conflicting/consumed experiment accounting and no immutable shared experiment lease was exposed to this organ; no duplicate unusual intervention was created. This receipt defines the ordinary acceptance discriminator only.

next_exact_step: After an exact-current PR810 deployment passes source guards, execute the bounded manual-snapshot lifecycle discriminator before spending the full Tier-2/Mistral recovery path. If lifecycle passes, continue exact declared-transfer/OCI/generation/effect/provider gates; if it fails, reject the snapshot carrier and evaluate only explicitly admitted independent durable carriers.
